title: Autoscaling Playbook and Failsafe Contracts for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Define and implement an operational playbook and machine-readable 'failsafe contract' for autoscaling policies on Dedicated fleets. Motivation: recent on-call incidents showed oscillation during workload spikes and two customer SLA breaches where burst buffer exhaustion caused extended throttling. We need a single source-of-truth policy format that encodes target metrics, prioritized scaling algorithms, and safety limits so fleet controllers and SRE runbooks behave predictably.

Scope: (1) policy DSL and schema for target_metric, scale_algorithm, safety_limits, cooldowns, and emergency_fallback. (2) Runtime enforcement hooks (reject unsafe configs) and compile-time vetting checks. (3) Playbook text for SRE and SEs: when to override, how to read guardrail telemetry, rollback steps. (4) Automated tests and chaos scenarios.

Links / artifacts: design sketch: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/autoscale-playbook; prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9812; incident postmortem: https://drive.redwood.ai/incidents/2024-11-dedicated-throttle-postmortem.pdf; example dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/throughput/autoscale-failsafe

Constraints & assumptions: must be compatible with existing routing fallback (model-variant fallback) and not require fleet restarts. Must operate within current telemetry sampling rates (1s for p50/p95, 1m for p99). Policy changes should be auditable and support canary rollouts.

Non-goals: building new ML predictors for demand forecasting in this ticket (we will consume forecast inputs produced by ENG-62345 later).
acceptance_criteria: Define a JSON Schema v1 for autoscale policy (target_metric, algorithm, params, safety_limits, cooldown, emergency_fallback)
Runtime validation: invalid or unsafe policies are rejected by the policy service with human-readable error codes
Controller implements at least two scaling algorithms (proportional-integral with slew limiter; quantile-based stepper) selectable per-policy
Safety limits enforced: max_scale_rate, max_replica_count, min_headroom, surge_quarantine and cross-tenant caps
Playbook doc created with clear runbook steps and example commands; reviewed by SRE and PM
20+ unit and integration tests covering edge cases; chaos test that triggers emergency_fallback succeeds in safe degraded mode
Telemetry added to console: per-policy scaling decisions, rejected policy attempts, safety-limit triggers, and canary rollout status
design_notes: Target metrics: support 'throughput_rps', 'per_tenant_token_rate', 'latency_p95', and composite metrics expressed as weighted sums. Accept both instantaneous and windowed (1m/5m) aggregations.

Algorithms: implement 'PI-slew' (PI controller with configurable integral windup and slew-rate limiter) and 'Quantile-stepper' (scale N replicas when observed p95 > target for M consecutive windows). Each algorithm exposes tunable params in the schema.

Safety limits: schema fields max_scale_rate (replicas/min), max_replicas, min_replicas, min_headroom_tokens, surge_quarantine_seconds. Controller must always honor tenant-level maxima and global safety gates.

Policy DSL: compact JSON with an optional human_description field. Example: {"target_metric":"throughput_rps","target_value":1200,"algorithm":{"type":"pi-slew","kp":0.12,"ki":0.02,"slew_rate":5},"safety_limits":{"max_replicas":50,"max_scale_rate":10}}

Validation: add static vetter that flags policies with contradictory constraints (e.g., target_value that requires >max_replicas) and suggests headroom adjustments. Vetter runs on the policy API and in CI for config-as-code PRs.

Telemetry / observability: emit policy_decision events with fields (policy_key, chosen_action, rationale, pre_metric, post_metric_estimate, safety_triggers). Integrate with Console for per-policy debugging and alerting thresholds.

Rollbacks and overrides: policies can be temporarily 'suspended' with an audit entry; emergency_fallback routes traffic to a lower-capacity but safer model variant and scales down new allocations while preserving token guarantees for in-flight requests.

Trade-offs: PI gives smooth behavior but can be slow to react under rapid ramp-ups; quantile-stepper is faster but may produce oscillations. Default policy will prefer PI-slew with conservative slew_rate and optionally enable stepper for public beta workloads requiring aggressive burst response.
rollout_plan: Week 0: merge JSON Schema + vetter + unit tests behind feature flag
Week 1: deploy controller changes to staging; run synthetic workloads to validate triggers and safety limits
Week 2: enable on 10% of Dedicated fleets as canary (non-production customer fleets), monitor policy_decision telemetry
Week 3: collect telemetry and tune default params; SRE runbook walkthrough and dry-run failures
Week 4: expand to 50% with automated rollback if safety triggers exceed threshold; prepare customer communication for upcoming behavior change
Week 5: full roll to GA and include policy editor in Console with read-only preview for affected fleets
test_plan: Unit tests for JSON schema and vetter code paths
Integration tests simulating various workload shapes: steady-state, sawtooth spikes, multi-tenant cold start, long-tail latency events
Chaos test: randomly delay scale actions and assert emergency_fallback maintains token guarantees for >=95% of in-flight requests
Performance test: ensure vetter and controller decision path add <5ms median latency to request path and controller can handle 10k policy decisions/hour
Safety regression suite that replays previous incident traces and asserts no SLA breach in staging
